title: Investigate and mitigate latency erosion affecting TTFT and tokens/sec across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple customers reported increased time-to-first-token (TTFT) and reduced tokens/sec across several models and deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private). Spike started ~2026-03-09 22:00 UTC and persisted with intermittent relief windows. Initial signals show higher scheduling latency between coalescer and kernel scheduler and increased KV cache miss amplification for long-context workloads. Impact: interactive chat experiences timing out for priority customers (FinEdge, ComposeAI evaluation), degraded SLAs on Dedicated pools, and Private clusters showing elevated tail latency during cross-variant fanout.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Measured TTFT for affected calls returns to baseline (+/-5% of pre-incident median) across hosted and dedicated within 24h of patch.
2) No regressions introduced in throughput (tokens/sec) for small-context workloads after fix.
3) Canary rollout shows stable behavior for private deployments with no errors for 2k requests over 1 hour.
4) Post-deploy dashboards updated and an automated alert created for the new signal (scheduler-queue-latency > 200ms).
reproduction_steps:
1) Run synthetic workload matching customer traffic: 20% long-context (>=2048 tokens), 60% short-context (<=128 tokens), 20% batching bursts.
2) Deploy model variants used by customers (open-model-7b-int8, open-model-13b-qat) in both hosted and dedicated pools.
3) Observe scheduler and coalescer metrics: queue length, dequeue latency, kernel selection duration, KV cache hit/miss ratios.
4) Trigger fanout test across two variants to reproduce cross-variant serialization delays.
5) Compare TTFT and tokens/sec against pre-2026-03-09 baselines.
work_notes: 2026-03-10 02:10 UTC - Pager: Customer FinEdge reported >2s TTFT increase on hosted; engaged SRE and on-call runtime team (Aisha, Marco).
2026-03-10 02:45 UTC - Initial triage: observed scheduler-queue-latency spike correlated with kernel selector thrashing during variant probing. KV cache miss ratio increased for priming requests.

2026-03-10 04:00 UTC - Mitigation: emergency traffic steering applied for FinEdge to fallback variant with aggressive prefetched KV snapshot (route -> variant A-stable). Immediate TTFT improved ~30% for the customer. Documented in incident channel.
2026-03-10 07:20 UTC - Hypothesis: a recent kernel selection heuristic (merged in PR 9362) misprioritized small-context requests causing preemption and longer first-token scheduling.
2026-03-10 09:00 UTC - Reproduction: synthetic harness reproduced the TTFT delta when scheduling heuristic enabled, particularly under mixed-context load.
2026-03-10 11:15 UTC - Patch created: revert selector heuristic and add guarded flag (selector_v2_enable) + metric gating. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9421.
2026-03-10 13:10 UTC - Canary deploy in us-west-hosted pool to 5% traffic. Observed median TTFT drop to baseline and tokens/sec restored for canary traffic. No errors observed in 30m window.
2026-03-10 15:00 UTC - Expanded rollout to dedicated pools with staged ramp. Private customers given advance notice and toggle to opt into selector_v2_enable=false for immediate relief.

2026-03-11 01:30 UTC - Follow-up: Implemented KV prefetch budget increase for long-context priming paths to reduce miss amplification during warmup. Disabled aggressive fanout probing when kernel selection under load. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9432.
2026-03-11 10:00 UTC - Monitoring: New alert added for scheduler-queue-latency and kernel-selection-count anomalies. Dashboard link: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/runtime/ttft-incident-818283.
2026-03-12 09:40 UTC - Customer comms: Sent interim update to FinEdge and ComposeAI describing mitigation and expected next steps. Scheduled joint validation window for 2026-03-14.
2026-03-12 11:00 UTC - Next steps: finalize automated rollback switch, harden selector unit tests for mixed-context traces, and author post-incident analysis doc.
